name: Proxy
intent: Put a stand-in object in front of another to control access: delay its creation, cache results, check permissions or log calls.
scenario: A photo gallery shows images. Loading a photo from disk is slow, so a proxy loads each one only when it is first displayed, and reuses it afterwards.
problem: Creating a RealImage loads the file immediately. A gallery with 100 photos loads all 100 at startup, even though the user looks at three. Startup is slow and memory is wasted.
solution: Create an ImageProxy with the same interface as the real image. It stores only the filename. On the first display() it creates the RealImage, then delegates. Later calls reuse the loaded image. The gallery cannot tell the difference.
pain: All images load at startup, used or not
Startup time grows with the size of the gallery
The gallery code is tangled with loading concerns
benefits: Opening the gallery is instant: only proxies are created
A photo loads on first view, once
The gallery uses the same Image interface for both
Lazy loading is isolated in one class
whenToUse: Lazy initialisation of expensive objects (virtual proxy)
Access control or permission checks (protection proxy)
Caching, logging, or talking to a remote object as if it were local
whenNotToUse: The object is cheap or always needed
Extra indirection would hide an important cost from callers
A simple cache or lazy variable would do the same job
pitfalls: Latency moves to the first use, which can surprise users
A proxy that does too much becomes hard to reason about
Must keep the same interface, or clients can tell it apart
Easy to confuse with Decorator: a proxy controls access, a decorator adds behaviour

roles.label: Subject
roles.description: The interface shared by the real object and its proxy.

roles.label: Proxy
roles.description: Same interface; controls access and creates the real object when needed.

roles.label: Client
roles.description: Uses the subject interface and never knows which one it holds.

quiz.question: A gallery screen creates 100 image proxies that each store only a file name and share the Image interface with the real image. The user opens the gallery, scrolls to photo 7 and displays it twice. How many files are read from disk?
options: One on each display call, so photo 7 is read twice
One, on the first display, then the loaded image is reused
100 at startup, because every proxy must be ready before the gallery opens
Seven, because scrolling to photo 7 passes six earlier photos that must load first
quiz.explanation: The proxy defers creating the real image until display() is first called, then keeps it. Startup creates only light proxies. Scrolling past a proxy does not load it unless it is displayed.

quiz.question: A billing service exposes an Invoice interface. Only users with the admin role may call it, the check must not touch the real service code, and callers should not change. Rejected calls must not even build the expensive real service. What fits best?
options: A protection proxy with the same interface that checks the role, then builds the real service
An adapter that converts Invoice calls into the admin API, so only admins know the new method names
A facade with fewer methods, which hides the dangerous operations from every caller
A permission check at the top of every method of the real service, which is simply guarded
quiz.explanation: A proxy with the same interface can run the check and decide whether to build or call the real object, with no client change. An adapter changes the interface, which breaks callers. A facade simplifies but does not check who is calling, and edits inside the real service are exactly what the requirement rules out.

quiz.question: A remote pricing client is wrapped in a proxy with the same interface as a local object. A checkout loop calls getPrice(sku) for 500 items. Each call is a 20 ms network round trip, so the page takes about 10 seconds. What is the lesson and the best fix?
options: Wrap the proxy in a second proxy that logs every call, so slow loops become visible in production dashboards and alerts
Keep the loop as is, because the proxy is meant to make remote calls cost the same as local calls
Swap the proxy for a decorator, which adds behaviour without hiding where the call is going
The identical interface hid a network cost, so add a batch call to the interface and fetch all prices at once
quiz.explanation: A proxy that looks like a local object can hide latency from callers, which is a known downside. A batch operation turns 500 round trips into one. Logging only shows the problem, and a decorator would still make 500 calls.
